headline: Highest risk is Dify’s broad server-side execution and shared datastore, but the pair with Whisper shows no direct prompt-injection or data-sharing channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest files and tool outputs, but Whisper has no write, network, clipboard, or MCP surface and is not an interactive agent. There is no documented shared communication channel where Whisper could inject instructions into Dify by default, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF Whisper is wrapped in a separate agent that writes text into Dify prompts or shared files, injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep Whisper outputs as plain transcripts, not instructions.
Do not auto-feed Whisper text into Dify system prompts.
Require human review before copying transcripts into Dify.
Store Whisper artifacts in a separate folder from Dify prompt assets.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs, knowledge base content, and secrets, while Whisper only handles audio/speech and has no filesystem read or network egress. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated cloud path, so leakage is limited to unusual operator wiring rather than default behavior.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are copied into Dify knowledge bases containing secrets, those secrets may be exposed in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Separate sensitive Dify workspaces from transcription workflows.
Redact secrets before importing transcripts.
Disable automatic indexing of Whisper outputs into knowledge bases.
Review Dify logs for sensitive transcript content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has write_filesystem and broad network egress, while Whisper has no write, no subprocesses, and no network. Their capabilities do not overlap on mutable resources, so direct conflict is unlikely; the main risk is only if an operator places both on the same writable directory, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF both are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering or stale reads can occur.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Mount Whisper inputs read-only.
Avoid concurrent writes from Dify to audio-processing folders.
Add filename prefixes per agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can act on tool outputs and workflow apps, so if Whisper transcripts are treated as authoritative, transcription errors can cascade into incorrect prompts, KB entries, or actions. Whisper is not a verifier, and Dify’s orchestration model makes this a default integration hazard even without malicious intent.
conditions: IF Dify consumes Whisper transcripts without a verification step, transcription mistakes propagate into downstream actions.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before Dify acts on transcripts.
Mark Whisper output as untrusted text.
Use confidence thresholds for low-quality audio.
Log source audio alongside derived text.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify handles conversation logs, knowledge base content, and secrets, while Whisper handles audio/speech. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, and Whisper is open-source/local by profile, so compliance risk is mainly from operator handling of audio containing regulated data rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated audio is transcribed into Dify without a retention or access policy, compliance gaps may arise.
mitigations: Classify audio before transcription.
Set retention limits for transcripts.
Restrict access to Dify logs and KB content.
Avoid storing regulated audio in shared workspaces.
